sentences.text: Lighted lateral buoys usually aren’t nun or can shaped.
They’re pillar or spar buoys, so you identify them by color, number and light.
A red mark shows a red light and a green mark shows a green light.
Lateral lights use flashing, occulting, quick or isophase rhythms.
A quick-flashing light often marks a sharp turn, a junction, or a spot needing special caution.
A preferred channel mark shows a composite group-flashing light, two flashes followed by one, in the color of its top band.
Unlighted buoys carry reflective tape in the mark’s color, so a spotlight at night can identify them.
